newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers' unions call Sept 27 strike.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers' unions call Sept 27 strike.

text.p: Italian unions representing 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers decided on Monday to call an eight-hour strike for September 27 in support of their pay claim, a joint statement by the unions said.

It will be the first nationwide strike over wage contracts in the sector since November 1990. Union leaders are due to meet the employers' organisation Federmeccanica on Thursday for the first time since negotiations were suspended in July.
A statement announcing Monday's decision by the FIOM, FIM and UILM unions blamed intransigence by Federmeccanica for blocking a deal on renewal of contracts, which expired in June.

The unions want an overall wage rise of around 10 percent for the next two years. This includes compensation for a loss of purchasing power of around four percent for June 1994-June 1996, plus six percent to cover forecast inflation in 1996 and 1997.
According to Michele Figurati, director-general of Federmeccanica, employers have offered a range of increases of between seven and nine percent in line with other contracts already renewed.
Industrialists say their markets have contracted and that rising labour costs coupled with recent rises in the value of the lire will wipe out past competitive gains.
